excerpt: Most facility managers treat tenant improvement renovation dust cleanup as a single pre-move-in event, only to battle clogged HVAC diffusers, chalky floors, and recurring white dust for months afterward. This scheduling and budgeting guide establishes exact remediation intervals based on occupancy foot traffic, active remodel phasing, and annualized per-square-foot spend.
quickAnswer: For a standard one-time office remodel, tenant improvement renovation dust cleanup should be scheduled in three timed intervals—an initial rough/final turnover clean ($0.22 to $0.35/sq ft), a 72-hour post-HVAC startup settling purge ($0.06 to $0.12/sq ft), and a 30-day overhead diffuser and carpet extraction pass ($0.08 to $0.14/sq ft). For growing corporate facilities undergoing continuous or phased tenant improvements across the calendar year, scheduling renovation dust remediation monthly (heavy churn/traffic), quarterly (moderate restacking), or semi-annually/annually (low churn) produces an annualized budget of $0.24 to $1.15 per square foot per year.

blocks.text: Why a Single Turnover Clean Never Captures 100% of Renovation Dust

Drywall joint compound, ceiling tile mineral fiber, and concrete core-drilling dust contain massive concentrations of sub-10-micron particulates. According to Stokes' Law of particle settling in still indoor air, a 10-micron gypsum particle takes roughly 8 minutes to fall 8 feet to the floor, whereas a 1- to 3-micron particle remains suspended for 12 to 36 hours—and is immediately re-entrained whenever HVAC blowers cycle on or employees walk down a corridor.

Even more significantly, up to 30% of airborne renovation dust hides inside drop-ceiling plenums, atop light troffers, inside return-air ductwork, and deep within carpet tile backing. As doors slam, HVAC dampers modulate between cooling and heating seasons, and foot traffic vibrates floor joists over the first 90 days post-construction, trapped particulate sheds continuously onto workstations. Facility managers who only fund a single pre-occupancy clean wind up fielding Indoor Air Quality (IAQ) complaints for an entire quarter.

blocks.text: The 3-Stage Post-Project Calendar for a One-Time Office Remodel

If your company is executing a single major tenant improvement project rather than continuous rolling renovations, structure your janitorial work order around three distinct calendar milestones rather than dumping 100% of the budget into Day Zero:

items.name: Day -2 (48 Hours Pre-Move-In): Full Top-to-Bottom Final Detail Clean
items.text: Once all punch-list trades have vacated and negative-air scrubbers are turned off, execute the primary HEPA high-to-low extraction, glass partition scraping, cabinet interior vacuuming, and two-bucket hard-floor rinse ($0.18 to $0.32 per square foot).

items.name: Day +3 (72 Hours After HVAC Full-Load Balancing): The Settling 'Puff' Purge
items.text: Run the suite's HVAC system at normal occupied fan speeds for 72 hours to flush out loose duct particulate, replace the MERV-13 return filters, and send a specialty crew after-hours to damp-wipe all horizontal desk planes, monitor arms, sills, and hard floors ($0.06 to $0.10 per square foot).

items.name: Day +30 to +45 (First Post-Occupancy Month): High-Diffuser & Carpet Deep Extraction
items.text: After four weeks of employee foot traffic have vibrated settled gypsum dust out of ceiling tracks and into carpet pile, perform an overhead supply-grille HEPA vacuum pass and deep hot-water carpet extraction or VCT scrub-and-recoat ($0.08 to $0.14 per square foot).

blocks.text: Scheduling Cadence by Foot-Traffic and Corporate Restacking Frequency

In multi-tenant commercial buildings, healthcare administration centers, and high-growth headquarters, tenant improvement dust isn't a once-a-decade event. Neighboring suites undergo demolition, internal teams reconfigure conference pods every quarter, and cabling contractors pop ceiling tiles weekly. Match your remediation calendar to your building's operational intensity:

items: Heavy Foot Traffic & Active Phased Construction (Monthly Remediation): When a company renovates a 25,000-square-foot floor in four occupied 6,250-square-foot quadrants over six months, employee shoes and air currents carry drywall dust across plastic zipper doors daily. Scheduling a monthly weekend HEPA high-dust and hard-floor neutralized wash (at the 1.28x monthly frequency multiplier or amortized into a project retainer at $0.10–$0.16/sq ft) prevents silica grit from scratching new LVT wear layers.

Medium Foot Traffic & Quarterly Space Restacks (Quarterly Remediation): Offices that add glass huddle rooms, shift modular walls, or sit adjacent to active landlord spec-suite build-outs benefit from a quarterly dust remediation calendar aligned with quarterly deep floor care ($0.03 to $0.06 per square foot per month amortized, plus $0.08 to $0.12 per square foot for quarterly high-surface HEPA extraction).

Low Foot Traffic & Static Layouts (Semi-Annual / Annual HVAC Changeover Clean): Even after a renovation is six months old, the first week the building switches from chilled-water cooling to winter heating blasts dried plenum dust out of ceiling registers. Scheduling a targeted semi-annual or annual overhead and horizontal dust purge every November keeps indoor particulate counts low.

blocks.title: Coordinate Dust Purges with Quarterly Deep Floor Care
blocks.text: Never schedule carpet hot-water extraction or VCT floor finish recoating BEFORE an overhead renovation dust purge. Always schedule high dusting of ceiling vents, pendant lights, and door headers on Friday night, and run your quarterly deep floor care ($0.03 to $0.06/sq ft/month amortized) on Saturday morning so settled dust is extracted rather than sealed under fresh floor wax.
Containment Matting and Low-VOC Disinfection Between Scheduled Purges

During phased renovations or the 30-day settling window after a build-out, up to 75% of cross-zone dust contamination is tracked by foot from construction corridors, freight elevator lobbies, and loading docks into finished office zones. Facility managers can stretch the interval between costly specialty cleanups from weekly to monthly by deploying commercial water-dam entrance matting at every zone boundary and switching daily porters to non-fuming peroxide cleaners.

At the primary transition doors between renovated wings and active corridors, laying down the Crown Mats 4x8 Charcoal Commercial Water-Trap Entrance Mat (featuring an oversized 4x8 ft footprint, beveled Rubber Border, molded Water-Dam cleats, and High Traffic polypropylene pile that traps dry drywall grit and up to 1.5 gallons of moisture per square yard) stops fine construction powder from reaching interior carpeting. For executive elevator lobbies and glass conference thresholds where aesthetic presentation matters, the M+A Matting WaterHog Fashion 4x6 Commercial Mat (built in a 4x6 ft profile with crush-resistant Pet-Fiber ridges, 45% Recycled content, and NFSI Cert high-traction backing) captures shoe-borne silica dust before it abrades hardwood or LVT floors. When day porters damp-wipe dusty desks and breakroom counters during occupied business hours, diluting CloroxPro Hydrogen Peroxide Cleaner Disinfectant Concentrate (supplied in a 128 oz Gal bottle with a fast Hydrogen Perox surfactant system, 1-Min Kill contact time, and No VOC Fumes duty profile) removes fine gypsum film and sanitizes high-touch surfaces without triggering respiratory irritation among newly relocated staff.
How Phased Renovation Schedules Impact Your Ongoing Monthly Cleaning Contract

When planning your annual facility budget, remember to account for how ongoing maintenance frequencies interact with renovation remediation. Standard commercial janitorial contracts bill across 4.33 weeks per month: a 2x-week schedule equals 8.66 visits per month (1.00x base multiplier), a 3x-week schedule equals 13.0 visits per month (0.95x multiplier), and a 5x-week daily weekday schedule equals 21.65 visits per month (0.90x multiplier).

If your office normally operates on a 2x-week or 3x-week schedule ($0.09 to $0.15 per square foot per visit for a 2,500–9,999 sq ft suite), temporarily upgrading your routine service to 5x-week for the first 30 days following a major renovation—or adding a quarterly amortized deep-clean rider ($0.03 to $0.06 per square foot per month)—is often 25% cheaper than booking emergency one-off specialty dispatches at the 1.28x monthly single-visit multiplier.

faqs.q: How long after a commercial office renovation does drywall dust continue to settle out of the air and ductwork?
faqs.a: While airborne room dust settles within 24 to 48 hours once construction ceases, secondary dust trapped inside drop-ceiling plenums, return-air grilles, light fixtures, and HVAC ductwork typically sheds for 30 to 90 days—and spikes again during the first seasonal switchover from air conditioning to heating. Scheduling a 72-hour post-HVAC purge and a 30-day high-diffuser detail pass captures over 95% of residual particulate.

faqs.q: Should we schedule daily or weekly dust remediation in occupied offices adjacent to an active remodel?
faqs.a: If employees are working in an adjacent zone separated only by plastic zipper barriers, schedule daily weekday (5x/week, 21.65 visits/month) HEPA vacuuming of walk-off mats and damp microfiber wiping of desks, paired with a monthly or biweekly (2.17 visits/month) high-reach overhead dust extraction until construction finishes.

faqs.q: How does the 4.33 weeks-per-month formula apply when amortizing quarterly post-renovation deep cleans?
faqs.a: When a janitorial vendor bundles quarterly high-dusting and deep floor extraction into your monthly retainer ($0.03 to $0.06 per square foot per month), they divide the four annual project events across 12 equal monthly invoices alongside your base recurring visits (which are calculated at 4.33 weeks per month, such as 13.0 visits/month for 3x/week service). This eliminates lumpy quarterly cap-ex spikes on your P&L.

faqs.q: When is the best time to change commercial HVAC filters after an office renovation cleanup?
faqs.a: Replace HVAC return filters twice: first, immediately after the Phase 2 final detail clean so construction-loaded filters do not restrict airflow; and second, 72 hours to 7 days later right after running the fans continuously and completing the post-settling 'puff clean.' Waiting until the normal quarterly filter cycle forces freshly cleaned offices to breathe air pulled through gypsum-caked filter media.
